judge: Nora — self-published romantic-fantasy novelist, eleven books, running the business solo, phone-first, not technical
first_five_minutes:
I open it on my phone in the kitchen. "Good morning, Cassandra." in that Cormorant italic — I actually smiled. The sidebar says Kira Stanley, Cassandra's author workspace, which is exactly right; nobody has split me into two people. Every made-up number wears a DEMO tag and the Instagram card says "Snapshot date unknown · Not live" instead of pretending. That buys enormous goodwill in ten seconds — I have never had a dashboard tell me its own numbers are fake.

I go to my Desk because that's the word that sounds like mine. Three briefs. I open one and immediately squint: the actual brief text — the thing I have to read to decide — is set at 11px on my phone (globals.css:2537). I pinch-zoom. I hit Approve; the dialog tells me plainly it is final, read-only, and that nothing gets published or sent. Good. I believe it.

Then I go to The Universe and open Assassin's Refusal, because a manuscript is the reason I would ever pay for this. The "What happens to your file" panel is the best thing in the app and the worst news in the app, in the same four bullets: Raven reads it in small steps, spoilers stay hidden, it's never rewritten — and "Every version you upload is kept. Removing a manuscript from the app isn't available yet — ask your workspace owner if you need a file removed." I am the author. The owner is Michael. So the sentence reads: once you hand us your unpublished book, you cannot take it back without asking your friend the developer. And the bullet above it tells me everyone with workspace access can read its passages, then links me to Workspace access to see who — and when I click, as an Editor, I get my own role description and nothing else (access-page.tsx:127). It tells me people can read my manuscript and then won't tell me who they are. I do not upload the file. I close the tab.

That is the five minutes. Everything about the craft says "somebody built this for me." The three sentences that matter most say "but it isn't yours yet."

scores.verdict: The everyday controls are hers — defaults favour her, nothing runs without a click, viewer/editor gates are explained kindly. But on the three things that actually matter to an author's ownership she is structurally the junior party: she cannot remove a manuscript or a book, she cannot see who has access to her own work, and she cannot approve her own marketing plan. The app is honest about each; it just doesn't hand her the keys.

scores.verdict: The strongest thing about this product. Every synthetic number is badged, the roadmap modules say "No live data has been collected and no agent is running here", the specialists card says "Not running. Not pretending to", Teach Raven explicitly denies retraining, approvals explicitly deny publishing, Ask Raven prints its model and estimated cost, access grants say "No invitation or email was sent", and the export warns it cannot be re-imported. I trust this app's self-description more than any tool I use. The crack is small but it is exactly where trust matters: a claim about who can read my manuscript that the app then refuses to substantiate.

top_findings.title: She is told who can read her manuscript, sent to check, and shown nothing
top_findings.problem: The "People with access" card is gated on `access?.role === "owner"`. Cassy is an Editor. Meanwhile desk-page.tsx:76, connected-book-detail.tsx:144 and connected-book-detail.tsx:168 all tell her that everyone with workspace access can read her briefs, her manuscript passages and its findings, and each links her to /access to see who. For her role that page shows only her own role description and "Private access details are not available right now." The app makes a factual claim about who reads her unpublished book and then declines to answer it.
top_findings.proposed_change: Change the gate to `{mode === "connected" && access && <div className="access-grid">` so the member list renders for every role; keep the Add-an-existing-account card and the per-member role select / Remove access buttons inside an inner `access.role === "owner"` check. Optionally surface a "Readable by N people in this workspace" count inline on the book page.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether editors/viewers may see collaborator email addresses. If not, show count + roles without emails — but do not leave the link dead.

top_findings.title: A manuscript, once uploaded, can never be withdrawn from the app
top_findings.problem: "Every version you upload is kept. Removing a manuscript from the app isn’t available yet — ask your workspace owner if you need a file removed." There is no DELETE route under app/api/manuscripts or app/api/library (only app/api/connections has one). The consent checkbox at line 148 is therefore irrevocable through the product: the author's only route to removing her own unpublished book is asking the developer.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add DELETE /api/manuscripts/[id] removing the stored file, chunks, embeddings and extracted knowledge under RLS, and a "Withdraw this version" action on each entry of the custody list (line 169) behind a confirmation dialog that names the file and states exactly what is destroyed and that it cannot be undone. Retain the append-only audit event.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: The SQL/storage cascade and whether withdrawal is hard delete or tombstone — an owner decision. The route, UI and dialog are code.

top_findings.title: An expired session silently discards plan, book and result forms it promised to hand back
top_findings.problem: `hasPrivateDrafts` counts only the desk scratchpad, learn drafts, the studio question and brief edits. PlanForm (plans-page.tsx:67), BookMetadataForm (connected-library.tsx:15) and the result-snapshot form (plans-page.tsx:134) hold state in plain useState. A 401 on any of their requests reaches library-provider.tsx:35 → endSession(); with no other draft open, demo-store.tsx:238 does `window.location.replace("/login")` with no dialog. A long plan intent, six goals and a budget vanish. When the dialog does open, session-ended-dialog.tsx:87 claims "your unfinished words are below, exactly as you left them" while listing none of them. plans-page.tsx:88 meanwhile tells her they are "Kept in this tab until you save."
top_findings.proposed_change: Add `registerDraft(key, label, getText)` / `releaseDraft(key)` to the workspace store; include registered non-empty drafts in `hasPrivateDrafts` and in the `kept` list built at session-ended-dialog.tsx:29. Register from PlanForm, BookMetadataForm and the result form while dirty. As an immediate stopgap, change plans-page.tsx:88 to "Not saved yet · These fields are lost if you reload or your session ends."

top_findings.title: The text she must read before an irreversible approval is the smallest on the page
top_findings.problem: `.approval-draft pre` renders the proposed brief at `var(--text-xs)` (11px), and globals.css:2538 pins it to 11px on phones too. This is the content she has to read carefully before pressing Approve, which approval-card.tsx:151 correctly warns is final and read-only. Around it, headings run 28–42px. The knowledge workbench has the same problem at 10px for `.knowledge-proof` (library.css:90), the label that distinguishes "Manuscript-supported" from "Interpretation".
top_findings.proposed_change: Set `.approval-draft pre` to 14px / line-height 1.8 and delete the mobile override at globals.css:2538. Raise `.knowledge-proof` and `.knowledge-index small:last-child` from 10px to 12px in library.css.

top_findings.title: Dark theme is forced on every viewer regardless of their system setting
top_findings.problem: `<html lang="en" className="dark">` is hard-coded; there is no `prefers-color-scheme` handling and no toggle anywhere in Settings. For a phone-first user working in daylight, or anyone who sets light mode for contrast reasons, there is no way out.
top_findings.proposed_change: Read a persisted preference plus `prefers-color-scheme` to set the class, add a theme control to settings-page.tsx, and add a light token block overriding the `:root` variables at globals.css:9-36 — plus an audit of the ~40 hard-coded hex values in globals.css and library.css that bypass the tokens.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether to ship a light palette at all before tomorrow's demo — the token work is mechanical but the hard-coded hex audit is not trivial.

top_findings.title: The author cannot approve her own marketing plan, and the UI has no path to ever make her owner
top_findings.problem: Only `role==="owner"` sees the review card (line 131) and the Activate action. As an Editor, Cassy gets a card that says her plan is "Waiting on owner review". The copy handles it gracefully ("a check on audience, budget and dates, not on you"), but access-page.tsx:12 restricts MemberRole to editor|viewer, so the product cannot transfer ownership to her either — the workspace named after her pen name can never be hers.
top_findings.proposed_change: Either add owner to MemberRole with an explicit transfer-ownership confirmation, or add one sentence on /access naming how ownership moves. Separately, give the non-owner a "Request a review" action that records a timestamped request, and allow activating dated tasks on a zero-budget plan without owner sign-off.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Who may approve marketing plans, and whether ownership transfers to Cassy — both role decisions for Michael. How the gate is explained and whether a review can be requested are code.

top_findings.title: Consent copy for the manuscript is written in engineer, at the exact moment she is deciding
top_findings.problem: The second bullet of "What happens to your file" reads "Passages are sent through Vercel AI Gateway to google/gemini-3.8-flash for reading and openai/text-embedding-3-small for search, under those providers’ terms." Naming the processor is correct and should stay. Printing raw model slugs mid-consent is where a non-technical author stops reading — and this is the one list in the product she most needs to finish.
top_findings.proposed_change: Rewrite as "Passages are read by Google's Gemini and searched with an OpenAI text index, both through Vercel's AI Gateway, under those providers' terms." and put the exact IDs in a `<details>` labelled "Exact models" directly beneath.

top_findings.title: Breadcrumb separator fails AA contrast on desktop
top_findings.problem: `.breadcrumb-divider { color: #606950; }` on the #121410 topbar measures 3.25:1 at 11px, below the 4.5:1 required by 1.4.3. It is hidden below 1100px (globals.css:3353), so it only fails at desktop widths — including the 1440px Playwright project.
top_findings.proposed_change: Change to `color: #9aa287;` (≈6.5:1), or render the separator as a non-text element and mark it aria-hidden.

what_works: Provenance is not a badge, it is a discipline. Every synthetic record carries DEMO, manual numbers carry MANUAL SNAPSHOT with "Snapshot date unknown · Not live" (mission-control.tsx:164-165), sourced titles carry PUBLIC SOURCE, and unknown metadata says NEEDS VERIFICATION rather than being quietly filled in. lib/knowledge/provenance.ts:22 refuses to let demo evidence support a non-demo finding at the type level. I have never used an author tool that was this unwilling to flatter itself.

The specialists card says "Not running. Not pretending to." (agent-status.tsx:19) and the roadmap routes say "This module is a roadmap preview. No live data has been collected and no agent is running here." (app/[module]/page.tsx:141). Refusing to fake an agent dashboard is the most trustworthy design decision in the product.

Draft protection around the Desk is genuinely best-in-class. Unsaved rewrites are stored keyed to the draft version they were written against (demo-store.tsx:135-143) so a newer draft cannot silently swallow her words; approval-card.tsx:156 even tells her "You wrote them against Draft 2; this brief is now Draft 3." A lapsed session opens a dialog that hands the text back with Copy buttons instead of clearing it (session-ended-dialog.tsx). Signing out with unsaved work asks first, and the destructive button is labelled "Sign out and discard drafts" rather than "OK".

The unreadable-demo-file dialog (session-ended-dialog.tsx:113-136) is the kind of thing almost nobody builds: "It has not been changed or deleted, and nothing is saved over it until you choose. Download a copy if you want it, then start fresh." That is what respecting someone's data actually looks like.

Irreversibility is stated before the click, not after. approval-card.tsx:151 and :214 both say the decision is final and the brief becomes read-only, and both say plainly that nothing will be published, sent, purchased or changed outside the workspace. The confirm dialog opens with focus on Cancel (approval-card.tsx:198), not on the destructive action.

Spoiler handling is thoughtful rather than performative: hidden by default, with a live count of exactly how many findings are being withheld (book-knowledge.tsx:89), a separate opt-in before any manuscript excerpt is searchable (connected-book-detail.tsx:166), and the spoiler setting recorded into any brief she saves to her Desk (book-knowledge.tsx:80).

"Teach Raven" tells the truth about itself — "Your guidance is saved for future use; it does not retrain a model" (approval-card.tsx:216) — and the desk sidebar repeats it. Refusing the easy AI-magic claim is worth a lot.

Every idea shelf, book page and Ask Raven handoff checks for an unfinished draft before overwriting it and offers "Keep my draft" / "Replace" with "Nothing changes until you choose" (manual-review-form.tsx:145, book-detail.tsx:216, book-details-brief.tsx:24, book-knowledge.tsx:105). Consistent, and consistently in her favour.

Access grants say "Access saved. No invitation or email was sent" and removals say "Workspace access removed. Their saved work is retained" (access-page.tsx:89-91). No growth-hack invitations, no signup funnel on /login, no dark pattern anywhere I could find.

The visual language is real design work, not a template: Cormorant Garamond against Manrope, a warm olive-gold dark palette, generous line-height, the raven line drawing, the inspiration reel with keyboard arrow support and a live position announcement. It looks like a place a novelist would want to spend time, which is not nothing — Vellum and Canva aside, nothing in my toolchain does.

Accessibility has been worked, not audited: focus returns to the exact trigger after every dialog, error paragraphs take focus, status and alert live regions are kept separate, the manuscript progress bar carries aria-valuetext in passages rather than percentages, and a reduced-motion block kills the smooth scroll. Four routes are held clean by axe in CI.

Ask Raven shows its model and estimated cost on every saved answer (studio-page.tsx:212), keeps the original answer unchanged when she copies it to her desk, and refuses to overwrite an unfinished question without asking. The demo mode shows example questions and states flatly "Nothing here calls a model."
